author: G. R. Mcclanahan
title: Analysis: 35 of 49 students at Grandview-Hopkins ISD's only school not on college track in 2024-25
text:
Of the 49 students in Grandview-Hopkins ISD’s only school, 35 (71%) were not on track for college in the 2024-25 school year, according to Amarillo Gazette’s analysis of STAAR scores from the Texas Education Agency (TEA) .
The TEA considers students to be on track for college if they demonstrate mastery of the course content through the State of Texas Assessments of Academic Readiness (STAAR).
In the 2023-24 school year, the TEA noted that 41 students at Grandview-Hopkins ISD—equivalent to 83% of the student population—were not on the academic path to college eligibility. This contrasts with the 2024-25 school year, where the percentage stood at 71%, down 12% from the previous year.
Data shows that 32% (4) of Grandview-Hopkins ISD’s 13 Hispanic students, and 29% (9) of its 34 white students had mastered their grade level in the 2024-25 school year and were “on track for college and career readiness,” as measured by state academic standards .
Primary data on overall student readiness in Grandview-Hopkins ISD is derived from the TSI assessments, which evaluate student capabilities in reading, writing, and mathematics. Certain students may qualify for exemptions from these assessments.
A 2026 study by WalletHub classified Texas as one of the least-educated states in the U.S. , ranking it 41st out of 50 in educational quality and student outcomes.
Texas has the nation’s second-largest K-12 public school system , serving about 5.5 million students with a student-to-teacher ratio of roughly 15:1.
